questions.q: What does SHOW TASKS reveal in this chapter's scenario?
options: A second, almost-identically-named Task, finance_refund_task_v2, still running alongside the original
That no Tasks exist in the schema at all
That the Stream itself has been deleted
That ticket_facts_sync_task is duplicated, not finance_refund_task
questions.explain: SHOW TASKS lists every existing Task — revealing the leftover finance_refund_task_v2 that was never suspended after an earlier change.

questions.q: What does TASK_HISTORY confirm about the two Finance Tasks?
options: Both show SUCCEEDED runs on the same schedule, with start times close enough to have genuinely overlapped
Only one of the two Tasks ever actually ran
finance_refund_task_v2 always fails with an error
The two Tasks ran on completely different schedules, a week apart
questions.explain: TASK_HISTORY shows both Tasks succeeding on overlapping schedules, confirming the hypothesis from SHOW TASKS.

questions.q: Mechanically, why did two overlapping Task runs produce duplicate refund_events rows?
options: A Stream's unconsumed rows stay visible to any transaction reading it until a commit happens, so both Tasks' MERGEs saw the same rows and both satisfied WHEN NOT MATCHED
Snowflake Streams automatically duplicate every row by default
The refund_amount column was defined with the wrong data type
finance_refund_task_v2 was reading from a different, corrupted Stream
questions.explain: Until a committing DML statement advances the offset, the Stream's data remains visible to other transactions — including a second, overlapping Task's MERGE.

questions.q: Why did Support's numbers stay correct while Finance's didn't, given both Tasks read the same Stream?
options: ticket_facts_sync_task was never duplicated, so it never hit the overlapping-execution problem that the duplicated finance_refund_task did
Support's view doesn't actually read from the same Stream at all
Support's numbers were also wrong, but nobody noticed
ticket_facts_sync_task runs on a completely different Stream
questions.explain: Only one instance of ticket_facts_sync_task exists, so there was no second consumer to create overlapping, duplicate-prone execution.

questions.q: Why does this lesson call the bug an "operational leftover" rather than a formula mistake?
options: finance_refund_task_v2's own MERGE logic is correctly written in isolation — the problem is that two copies of the same consumer existed and ran against one Stream at once
Because the MERGE statement contains an actual SQL syntax error
Because refund_amount was never cast to the correct type
Because the Stream itself was created with the wrong ON TABLE clause
questions.explain: Reviewing the MERGE statement's own logic would never reveal this bug — it's a leftover duplicate object, not a flaw in anyone's SQL.
